terms.title: Component
terms.definition: A reusable, self-contained UI building block in React.
terms.explanation: Components accept inputs called props and return React elements describing what should appear on screen.

terms.title: JSX
terms.definition: A syntax extension for JavaScript that allows writing HTML-like code inside JS.
terms.explanation: Compiles down to standard React.createElement calls via build tools like Babel.

terms.title: Props
terms.definition: Short for properties, these are read-only inputs passed to components.
terms.explanation: Allows child components to receive data and handlers from parent components.

terms.title: State
terms.definition: A plain JavaScript object used to record and react to user events or changes over time.
terms.explanation: When a component's state changes, React automatically re-renders the component.

terms.title: useState Hook
terms.definition: A React Hook that lets functional components maintain local state.
terms.explanation: Returns a pair: the current state value and a function to update it.

terms.title: useEffect Hook
terms.definition: A Hook that allows perform side effects in functional components.
terms.explanation: Handles operations like data fetching, DOM updates, and subscriptions.

terms.title: Dependency Array
terms.definition: The second argument passed to hooks like useEffect, useMemo, or useCallback.
terms.explanation: Tells React to re-run the effect only when specified values in the array change.

terms.title: Virtual DOM
terms.definition: A lightweight, in-memory representation of the real browser DOM.
terms.explanation: React compares this virtual representation to the real DOM to compute minimal UI updates.
terms.example: React reconciliation updates only changed node elements in the actual DOM.

terms.title: Reconciliation
terms.definition: The diffing algorithm React uses to determine which parts of a tree need to be updated.
terms.explanation: Compares new and previous Virtual DOM trees to execute minimal real DOM updates.
terms.example: Uses element keys to efficiently track node additions, movements, and deletions.

terms.title: Keys
terms.definition: A special string attribute required when creating lists of elements in React.
terms.explanation: Helps React identify which items have changed, been added, or been removed.

terms.title: useMemo Hook
terms.definition: A Hook that memoizes the result of a calculation between re-renders.
terms.explanation: Caches calculated values to prevent recalculation unless dependent values change.

terms.title: useCallback Hook
terms.definition: A Hook that memoizes a function definition between re-renders.
terms.explanation: Prevents unnecessary child component re-renders by preserving function identity.

terms.title: useRef Hook
terms.definition: A Hook that lets you reference a value that isn't needed for rendering.
terms.explanation: Commonly used for direct DOM node access or storing mutable instance variables without triggering re-renders.

terms.title: Context API
terms.definition: A feature for sharing data globally across the component tree without prop drilling.
terms.explanation: Composed of a Provider component and a consumer hook (useContext).

terms.title: useContext Hook
terms.definition: A Hook that reads and subscribes to context from a component.
terms.explanation: Grabs the current context value provided by the nearest matching Context.Provider.

terms.title: Prop Drilling
terms.definition: The process of passing props down through multiple layers of components to reach a deeply nested child.
terms.explanation: Often solved using Context API, state management libraries, or component composition.

terms.title: useReducer Hook
terms.definition: A Hook for managing complex state logic in functional components via actions and reducers.
terms.explanation: Alternative to useState when state transitions are complex or rely on previous state.

terms.title: Custom Hooks
terms.definition: Reusable JavaScript functions prefixed with 'use' that encapsulate hook logic.
terms.explanation: Allows sharing stateful logic between components without duplicating code.
terms.example: function useFetch(url) { /* fetch state logic */ return { data, loading }; }

terms.title: React.memo
terms.definition: A higher-order component that memoizes a functional component.
terms.explanation: Prevents re-renders if the component's props have not changed.

terms.title: Higher-Order Component
terms.definition: An advanced pattern in React for reusing component logic.
terms.explanation: A function that takes a component as an argument and returns a new enhanced component.

terms.title: Render Props Pattern
terms.definition: A technique for sharing code between React components using a prop whose value is a function.
terms.explanation: The component calls this prop function instead of implementing its own render logic.

terms.title: Fragment
terms.definition: Allows grouping a list of children without adding extra nodes to the DOM.
terms.explanation: Rendered via <React.Fragment> or shorthand syntax `<> ... </>`.

terms.title: Portals
terms.definition: A way to render children into a DOM node that exists outside the DOM hierarchy of the parent component.
terms.explanation: Commonly used for modals, tooltips, and floating popovers.

terms.title: Error Boundaries
terms.definition: React components that catch JavaScript errors anywhere in their child component tree.
terms.explanation: Logs errors and displays a fallback UI instead of crashing the entire component tree.
terms.example: Implemented using class components with componentDidCatch or getDerivedStateFromError.

terms.title: Suspense
terms.definition: A built-in React component that lets you display a fallback UI until its children finish loading.
terms.explanation: Works with asynchronous operations like dynamic imports (`React.lazy`) or concurrent data fetching.

terms.title: React.lazy
terms.definition: Lets you defer loading component code until it is rendered for the first time.
terms.explanation: Enables dynamic imports and code splitting in React applications.

terms.title: Strict Mode
terms.definition: A developer tool that highlights potential problems in an application.
terms.explanation: Intentionally double-invokes effects and renders in development to surface side effect bugs.

terms.title: Controlled Component
terms.definition: A form element whose value is controlled by React state.
terms.explanation: Changes to the input trigger state update handlers, serving as the single source of truth.

terms.title: Uncontrolled Component
terms.definition: A form element that maintains its own internal state in the DOM.
terms.explanation: Values are queried from the DOM using a ref instead of using event handlers for every state update.

terms.title: SyntheticEvent
terms.definition: A cross-browser wrapper around the browser’s native event.
terms.explanation: Normalizes event behavior across different browsers while providing the same interface as standard events.

terms.title: Server Components
terms.definition: Components that fetch data and render exclusively on the server.
terms.explanation: Reduces client bundle size and improves initial load performance by keeping dependencies server-side.
terms.example:
async function ServerCard() { const data = await db.query(); return
{data}
; }

terms.title: Client Components
terms.definition: Interactive components rendered on the client side in modern React framework setups.
terms.explanation: Explicitly declared using the `'use client'` directive; support state, effects, and event listeners.
terms.example: 'use client'; export default function Counter() { const [c, setC] = useState(0); }

terms.title: useActionState Hook
terms.definition: A modern Hook that updates state based on the result of a Form Action.
terms.explanation: Designed to simplify form submission handling, tracking pending states and return values natively.

terms.title: useFormStatus Hook
terms.definition: A Hook providing status information about the parent form submission.
terms.explanation: Allows child components to check pending status without manual prop passing.

terms.title: useOptimistic Hook
terms.definition: A Hook that allows optimistically updating UI while an async action is in flight.
terms.explanation: Instantly displays expected state while server mutations execute, rolling back if they fail.

terms.title: useId Hook
terms.definition: A Hook for generating unique IDs that are stable across server and client renders.
terms.explanation: Prevents hydration mismatch errors when wiring up accessibility attributes.

terms.title: Hydration
terms.definition: The process where React attaches event listeners to pre-rendered HTML sent by the server.
terms.explanation: Transforms static server-rendered HTML markup into a fully dynamic, interactive browser DOM tree.

terms.title: Code Splitting
terms.definition: Splitting JavaScript bundles into smaller chunks loaded on demand.
terms.explanation: Improves initial web application load time by avoiding heavy single-bundle downloads.
terms.example: Using dynamic imports via React.lazy() to route component bundles.

terms.title: useTransition Hook
terms.definition: A Hook that lets you mark state updates as non-blocking transitions.
terms.explanation: Keeps current UI responsive while rendering large updates in the background.

terms.title: useDeferredValue Hook
terms.definition: A Hook that lets you defer updating a non-critical part of the UI.
terms.explanation: Similar to debouncing, but integrated natively with React's concurrent rendering engine.

terms.title: useImperativeHandle Hook
terms.definition: A Hook that customizes the handle exposed as a ref to parent components.
terms.explanation: Used alongside forwardRef to limit what internal methods or nodes a parent can access.

terms.title: forwardRef
terms.definition: A method to pass a ref through a component to one of its children.
terms.explanation: Gives parent components direct access to DOM nodes inside child functional components.

terms.title: useInsertionEffect Hook
terms.definition: A Hook intended for CSS-in-JS library authors that fires before any DOM mutations.
terms.explanation: Injects styles into the DOM before layout reads or paint cycles execute.

terms.title: useLayoutEffect Hook
terms.definition: A version of useEffect that fires synchronously after all DOM mutations but before browser paint.
terms.explanation: Used to measure DOM layout dimensions to prevent visual flicker before the screen updates.

terms.title: Class Components
terms.definition: The legacy method of defining React components using ES6 JavaScript classes.
terms.explanation: Extends React.Component and uses lifecycle methods like componentDidMount.
terms.example:
class Welcome extends React.Component { render() { return

Hi

; } }

terms.title: Component Lifecycle
terms.definition: The series of phases a component passes through from birth to death.
terms.explanation: Phases consist of Mounting, Updating, and Unmounting.

terms.title: Unidirectional Data Flow
terms.definition: The architectural pattern where data flows in one direction from parent to child components.
terms.explanation: Ensures predictable state changes and makes component hierarchies easier to debug.
terms.example: Parents pass state to children via props; children request changes via passed callbacks.

terms.title: Children Prop
terms.definition: A special prop that allows components to pass elements nested between their opening and closing tags.
terms.explanation: Used to build generic container components that encapsulate structural layout.

terms.title: Pure Components
terms.definition: Components that render the exact same output for the exact same props and state.
terms.explanation: In functional React, components are pure when free of side-effects during render.

terms.title: Compiler
terms.definition: An build tool that automatically optimizes React code.
terms.explanation: Automatically memoizes components, props, and hooks at compile time, reducing the need for manual useMemo/useCallback.
terms.example: Automatically handles shallow value comparison optimization during compilation.
